sara: Quick heads-up: merged cust-quill LoRA to staging and ran the int4 smokepack on invoice samples. seeing a small upward bias on extracted amounts (~+0.02-+0.04).

evan: ouch. paste a tiny repro?

sara: run: python eval_pack/run_smoke.py --model quill-lora-int4 --dataset samples/invoices/seed-12.jsonl --metrics amount_exact_match
output:
{"id":"inv-101","pred_amount":"$58.03","gold":"$58.00"}
{"id":"inv-118","pred_amount":"$7.99","gold":"$7.95"}
{"id":"inv-130","pred_amount":"$0.00","gold":"$0.00"}

ciara: zeros ok suggests small additive shift from quantization not tokenizer. fp16 baseline passes?

sara: fp16 matches gold. int4 shows bias.

mike: runtime recently enabled per-channel fallback for some kernels. no tokenizer deltas in the merge.

ciara: run ablation: int4 with KV-cache off and int4 forcing 8-bit attention kernel.

bench-bot: qb-3789001234-ablation started (tags: [cust-quill,int4-bias])

sara: results: kv-cache off reduces bias (~+0.01) but doesn't remove it. forcing 8-bit attention kernel eliminates bias on this sample set.

mike: likely interaction between attention-kernel quantization and LoRA deltas (softmax scaling/underflow).

evan: plan: pin customer rollout to int8-attn kernel on Dedicated, add quick-eval to merge gate that asserts invoice rounding within +/- $0.01, and open kernel bug.

ciara: +1. add playbook note for new customer launches.

deploy-bot: canary blocked: "quantization-regression" check failed for redwood/cust-quill -> manual approval required.

mike: I'll reproduce locally, dump attention logits for numeric token spans, and file kernel issue if reproducible. ETA ~2h.

bench-bot: qb-3789001234-ablation finished; logs in /artifacts/qb-3789001234 (summary: int4->8bit-attn removed bias; kv-cache toggle partial improvement).

sara: added a tiny unit test in the quick-eval pack and updated the onboarding note: https://git.internal/redwood/cust-quill/merge-requests/114 :thumbsup:
